academicJudgment.strongestObjection: ST&I is an integrated scientific/engineering programme with sustained working-prototype training, not merely a collection of broad science topics. Its known Materials route has substantial condensed-matter, quantum/optical, thermodynamic and technical studio formation. Even the firstyear includes real mechanics, introductoryquantum, synthetic genome/network methods, chemicalfuel laboratories, farm/agrochemistry and weeklyMakerspace/microcontroller projects. Excluding later114EC cannot excuse falsely treating those included60EC subjects as covered. Mechanical24course feasibility, genericethics or degree-title avoidance do not establish meaningful comparability.
academicJudgment.decision: The adopted common object itself has four specific interdisciplinary scientific strands and applied modelling/design practices. The strengthened broad UCR response has actual chemical/wave/biopolymer/circular-material laboratories, molecular/cellular/biochemical teaching and transformation/PCR/protein/DNA work, scientificprogramming/matrix/modelling/data methods, real robot-arm manipulation, energy/lifecycle assessment and consumer-design specifications/testing. These are sustained actual taught subjects and methods that materially address that common scientific/technological object. They are not borrowed from optionalfuture research. The digital route is a genuinely narrower computing/robotics/model-validation response; the life-health route deepens molecular/biomedical/laboratory and experimental evaluation. Their distinct organising priorities are supported by exacttarget interests. This supports broader limited responses, not fullfirstyear equivalence or the unassessedMaterialsdegree.

readerValues.programmeDescription: Science, Technology & Innovation at the University of Amsterdam is a Dutch-taught programme combining natural sciences, data and modelling with the design and testing of technological prototypes. This example follows High-tech Designer Materials.
readerValues.comparisonExplanation: This qualified comparison assesses the confirmed 60 EC common first year of Science, Technology & Innovation. The three UCR programmes develop different combinations of material and biological science, computation, laboratory inquiry and technological design. They do not reproduce all physics, chemical energy, synthetic biology, web technology or sustained Makerspace fabrication and microcontroller training. All later specialisation, projects, final research and complete progression are excluded.

componentNotes.y1-58719: Builds mathematical, statistical and computational foundations and applies them to the programme’s scientific themes.
componentNotes.y1-61760: Studies food systems through nutrient and carbon cycles, agricultural chemistry, farm fieldwork, soil analysis and ethical and social questions.
componentNotes.y1-58696: Introduces computational thinking, algorithms and programming for scientific modelling and simulation.
componentNotes.y1-58958: Develops academic practices, teamwork and design skills, with workshops, a reflective portfolio and practical technical activities.
componentNotes.y1-59419: Introduces cellular building blocks, biochemistry and molecular processes, using microscopy and computational models.
componentNotes.y1-58679: Applies Newtonian mechanics to moving objects and a practical design-and-build task in the Makerspace.
componentNotes.y1-58798: Continues mathematical, statistical and computational skills in the context of second-semester scientific themes.
componentNotes.y1-58951: Develops client-server applications, databases, data cleaning and querying, and interactive web content using JavaScript.
componentNotes.y1-59418: Develops molecular cloning, genome-engineering and bioinformatics techniques through laboratory and computational work.
componentNotes.y1-58768: Continues academic practices, teamwork and technical development through workshops and reflective work.
componentNotes.y1-58799: Studies waves, oscillations, light and their interaction with matter, including the foundations of sensors and optical instruments.
componentNotes.y1-58702: Connects chemical bonding, thermodynamics and reaction kinetics to energy conversion, storage and practical energy technologies.
componentNotes.y2-58706: A compulsory team project follows the selected specialisation. Workshops and preparation run throughout the year, with execution in the final period. Practical participation requires the programme’s safety instruction. This component is outside the assessed 60 EC common first year.
componentNotes.y2-59420: Introduces bonding, crystal structure and electronic behaviour in condensed-matter and materials physics. This component is outside the assessed 60 EC common first year.
componentNotes.y2-58586: Develops vector calculus, eigenvalue methods, complex matrices and systems of differential equations for scientific modelling. This component is outside the assessed 60 EC common first year.
componentNotes.y2-58874: Applies machine learning to scientific problems, including computational representations of molecules and materials. This component is outside the assessed 60 EC common first year.
componentNotes.y2-58521: Combines electronics and photonics with circuit construction, simulation, measurements, filters and spectroscopy. This component is outside the assessed 60 EC common first year.
componentNotes.y2-58760: Develops statistical data analysis and Python programming using a realistic dataset. This component is outside the assessed 60 EC common first year.
componentNotes.y2-59430: Studies fluid and solid mechanics, viscosity, elasticity and viscoelastic behaviour across microscopic and macroscopic scales. This component is outside the assessed 60 EC common first year.
componentNotes.y2-58591: Examines telescopes, microscopes and detectors, linking optical and detector technology to scientific discovery and measurement. This component is outside the assessed 60 EC common first year.
componentNotes.y2-61794: Uses statistical thermodynamics to connect molecular behaviour to material properties, phase transitions and soft-matter systems. This component is outside the assessed 60 EC common first year.
componentNotes.y2-58830: Applies thermodynamics, quantum mechanics and electromagnetism to energy conversion and storage, including semiconductors and batteries. This component is outside the assessed 60 EC common first year.
componentNotes.y3-59335: A full-time eight-week team project develops a physical prototype through design, testing and ethical decisions. It ends with a demonstration, presentation and a partly individual defence. Entry requires the completed first year, at least 120 EC and the Design Project; practical work requires safety instruction. This component is outside the assessed 60 EC common first year.
componentNotes.y3-59417: An individual supervised research project includes a thesis and presentation and is examined by at least two UvA examiners. Entry requires the completed first year, at least 120 EC and the Design Project. External projects need Examination Board permission. This component is outside the assessed 60 EC common first year.
componentNotes.y3-open: Thirty EC remain open for electives or a minor, normally in the first semester of year three. The study plan is assessed for overlap and approval; at most 12 EC may be introductory subjects, and a foreign minor needs prior approval. This component is outside the assessed 60 EC common first year.
